sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Alok Mishra Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Pawan Kumar Shukla Hon'ble Mayank Kumar Jain,J.
Heard learned counsel for applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State and perused the record.

The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed praying for quashing the charge sheet dated 9.9.2021as well as entire criminal proceedings in Session Trial No. 83517 of 2021 under Section 498A, 323, 506 I.P.C. and 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S. Mahila Thana, District Ghaziabad arising out of Case Crime No. 58 of 2021.
It is further submitted that stay the further proceeding of the aforesaid case.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that all the disputes and differences have been settled between the parties.
The compromise was filed before the concerned court and vide its order dated 29.11.2023, it is brought on record, the compromise has been verified by the Court.

At this stage, learned counsel further submitted that continuation of the proceedings of the aforesaid case Divanshu vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65474861/
1 will be an abuse of process of law.

sentences.text: No fruitful purpose would be served keeping the matter pending.

In support of his contention, learned counsel for the applicant has also placed reliance on the law laid down by Apex Court in Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab, (2012), 10 SCC 303, B.S. Joshi and others vs. State of Haryana and another, (2003) 4 SCC 675 and Madan Mohan Abbot vs. State of Punjab, (2008) 4 SCC 582.
On the other hand, Mr. Pawan Kumar Shukla, learned counsel for the opposite party No. 2 submits that since the dispute between the parties has been settled, opposite party no.2 has no objection if the proceedings of the aforesaid complaint case pending before the trial court is quashed.

sentences.text: I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire record.

In all the aforesaid cases, the Apex Court has laid down the law that criminal proceedings may be quashed even in non-compoundable cases by the High Court in exercise of its extraordinary jurisdiction to restore peace between the parties and in case the justice so demands.

According to Hon'ble Supreme Court, if the offence involve private dispute between the parties of commercial nature or matrimonial dispute and it is not related to heinous offence, the proceedings may be quashed.

Since the dispute between the parties has been amicably and mutually settled, no fruitful purpose would be served by permitting to continue the criminal case pending before the trial court and it would simply be a waste of time if the aforesaid case is permitted to continue till its logical conclusion.
In view of the above, the Application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. is allowed.

The entire proceedings of Session Trial No. 83517 of 2021 under Section 498A, 323, 506 I.P.C. and 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S. Mahila Thana, District Ghaziabad arising out of Case Crime No. 58 of 2021 against the applicant are quashed in terms of compromise arrived at between the parties.
